docs.D01_business_overview.md:
Title: Long-lived industrial-gas infrastructure with uneven business mix
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2969/000119312512476878/d409668d10k.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2969/000119312513166085/d526189dex991.htm
Date: 2013-04-23

Air Products supplies industrial gases, performance materials, equipment and related technology. Its customers include refineries, chemical plants, steelmakers, electronics manufacturers, food processors and healthcare users. Fiscal2012 sales were approximately US$9.612 billion across more than50 countries.

The four reported segments are Merchant Gases, Tonnage Gases, Electronics and Performance Materials, and Equipment and Energy. They have different capital intensity and cyclicality; a single company-wide margin does not identify which activities explain a peer gap.

Merchant gases reach customers through bulk liquid deliveries, cylinders and smaller on-site systems. Local plant density, distribution efficiency, reliable service and pricing discipline matter. A customer's gas bill may be small relative to the cost of interrupted production, supporting durable supplier relationships.

Tonnage gases involve large on-site plants supplying oxygen, hydrogen and other gases under long-term arrangements. The installed plant and integration with customer operations create switching barriers. Contracts and energy pass-through can reduce certain risks, but utilization, customer outages, project execution and capital cost still matter.

Electronics and materials expose the group to semiconductor cycles and product-specific competition. Equipment and Energy includes LNG-related technology and equipment, with project timing rather than a smooth recurring delivery pattern.

Fiscal2012 segment sales were approximately US$3.662 billion Merchant, US$3.207 billion Tonnage, US$2.323 billion Electronics/Materials and US$420 million Equipment/Energy. Segment operating income was approximately US$644 million, US$512 million, US$426 million and US$45 million, before unallocated company items. Segment sums are not interchangeable with consolidated adjusted EBIT.

Chairman/CEO John McGlade emphasizes productivity, emerging-market projects and recovery leverage. The company has announced withdrawal from polyurethane intermediates, demonstrating that portfolio pruning is already possible without assuming a new activist's control.

An attractive franchise thesis rests on essential products, technical competence, installed assets and long-duration customer relationships. It does not imply every investment earns a good return. High project capex and acquisitions can absorb cash for years.

The main analytical question is whether the weaker group economics reflect business mix and geography or remediable operating/capital discipline. Leadership change or separation could be tools to investigate, but neither is an established post-cutoff outcome to assume in the valuation.
docs.D02_financial_snapshot.md:
Title: Strong cash generation, expensive expansion and adjustment discipline
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2969/000119312512476878/d409668d10k.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2969/000119312513166085/d526189dex991.htm
Date: 2013-04-23

US$ millions except EPS. Fiscal years end September30. Continuing operations use the original2012 filing perimeter, not a later post-separation restatement.

| Metric | FY2010 | FY2011 | FY2012 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Sales | 8,616 | 9,674 | 9,612 |
| GAAP operating income | 1,268 | 1,508 | 1,282 |
| Attributable continuing income | 942 | 1,134 | 999 |
| Continuing diluted EPS | 4.34 | 5.22 | 4.66 |
| Total net diluted EPS | 4.74 | 5.63 | 5.44 |
| Operating cash flow | 1,485 | 1,710 | 1,765 |
| Cash plant/equipment additions | 988.7 | 1,309.3 | 1,521.0 |
| Calculated CFO less plant additions | 496.3 | 400.7 | 244.0 |
| Declared dividend/share | 1.92 | 2.23 | 2.50 |

The apparent EPS choice matters: total net income includes discontinued operations. FY2012 adjusted continuing EPS was US$5.40 versus US$4.66 GAAP continuing. Do not compare US$5.44 total GAAP to the US$5.40 continuing adjusted figure and infer almost no adjustments.

FY2012 restructuring/cost-reduction charges were US$327.4 million, partly offset by an US$85.9 million gain on a previously held equity interest. Adjusted operating income was US$1.534 billion, 16.0% margin, versus reported13.3%. FY2011 adjusted margin was16.1%; the underlying gap is not just one year's restructuring expense.

Cash plant additions exclude acquisitions and other capital deployment. FY2012 issuer GAAP capital expenditures were US$2.560 billion; its broader non-GAAP measure was US$2.778 billion including capital-lease spending and other items. Simple CFO less plant additions is not cash left after all growth investment.

Share repurchases were US$649.2 million in2011 and US$53.1 million in2012. At March31 2013 cash was US$401.6 million. Debt comprised US$1,239.8 million short-term, US$96.7 million current long-term and US$4,644.7 million long-term, totaling US$5,981.2 million. Net debt is US$5,579.6 million, calculated.

Issuer adjusted return on capital employed was11.5% in2012 versus12.5% in2011. Clean maintenance/growth capex and a standardized ROIC bridge remain gaps; growing assets is not necessarily value creation.
docs.D03_latest_results_and_guidance.md:
Title: Acquisition-led sales growth masks weak underlying demand
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2969/000119312513166085/d526189dex991.htm; https://www.fool.com/investing/general/2013/04/24/air-products--chemicals-increases-sales-but-misse.aspx
Date: 2013-04-24

FiscalQ2, ended March31, is the latest published quarter at this cutoff. Air Products reports US$2.484 billion sales, up6% year over year, and US$289 million attributable continuing income, US$1.37 diluted continuing EPS.

The underlying sales comparison is negative2%, affected by the decision to exit polyurethane intermediates. Acquisitions contribute6%. Reported revenue growth therefore does not establish a volume recovery in the existing business.

Operating income is approximately US$390 million and margin15.7%, down30 basis points. The company attributes pressure to acquisitions and pension expense, partly offset by productivity. Sequential underlying sales decline3%, partly because of planned customer maintenance.

Merchant Gases sales rise14% to US$1.003 billion, largely from Indura, with operating income US$168 million. Underlying sales fall1% as positive pricing is outweighed by lower European and helium volumes. Distribution and energy costs also affect performance.

Tonnage sales rise3% to US$809 million and operating income is US$123 million. New plants and energy pass-through support revenue, while lower polyurethane volume and customer outages restrain growth. Electronics/Materials sales fall3% to US$549 million and operating income falls9% to US$78 million amid weak electronics demand and price pressure.

Equipment/Energy sales increase12% to US$124 million, with US$21 million operating income, supported by LNG activity. This project-driven improvement cannot simply be applied to all company sales.

The company guides Q3 adjusted continuing EPS to US$1.33–US$1.38 and FY2013 to US$5.45–US$5.60. Expected capital spending is approximately US$1.9–US$2.1 billion under its broader non-GAAP definition.

April24 Motley Fool coverage, citing S&P Capital IQ, gives Q2 revenue consensus US$2.60 billion and EPS consensus US$1.37. Its next-quarter EPS estimate is US$1.48 and next-year estimate US$5.71. These are dated observations, not verified July consensus.

The summary initially describes lower non-GAAP EPS against a US$1.39 prior-year number that includes discontinued earnings; the original company release instead reports5% growth in continuing EPS. The pack preserves that distinction rather than reproducing an inconsistent headline comparison. The next results must test volumes, acquisition returns and cash productivity, not just EPS adjustments.
docs.D04_price_and_valuation.md:
Title: A reasonable multiple requires a credible margin and capital bridge
Source: compiled from: https://exa.ai/library/markets/stock/APD?date=2013-07-15&view=daily; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2969/000119312512476878/d409668d10k.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2969/000119312513166085/d526189dex991.htm
Date: 2013-07-15

The historical July15 close is US$96.61. The archive gives session high/low US$96.76/US$96.15 and approximately1.14 million volume. Yahoo's historical series is retrospectively adjusted for corporate actions and is not used directly with original share counts or EPS.

An exact independently checked rolling52-week range and average volume in original share units remain unavailable here. The annual report gives fiscal2012 high/low US$93/US$72, a different period, not a rolling range to July2013.

Using approximately211 million diluted Q2 shares as an indicative denominator gives US$20.38 billion equity value. This is not a verified point-in-time basic capitalization. Adding March net debt US$5.580 billion gives approximatelyUS$25.96 billion enterprise value before minority/pension and other adjustments.

| Valuation basis | Calculated result |
|---|---:|
| FY2012 continuing GAAP EPS US$4.66 | 20.7x |
| FY2012 adjusted continuing EPS US$5.40 | 17.9x |
| FY2013 adjusted guidance US$5.45–US$5.60 | 17.3–17.7x |
| April next-year consensus US$5.71 | 16.9x |
| EV / FY2012 adjusted EBIT US$1.534bn | 16.9x |

These are approximate calculations, not company targets. The forward consensus is stale and should not be represented as a July15 live estimate. The quarterly dividend is US$0.71; four times this rate gives US$2.84 and an approximately2.9% indicated yield if maintained.

On FY2012 sales, each percentage point of margin is approximatelyUS$96 million EBIT. Praxair's Q1 adjusted margin21.6% versus APD's fiscalQ2 15.7% suggests a potentially valuable gap. It does not prove the entire difference is attainable: product mix, energy pass-through, geography and accounting differ.

The simple CFO less cash plant-additions yield is only approximately1.2% against this equity value. Expansion capex depresses it, but acquisitions and leases consume additional capital. Normalized capital returns matter as much as accounting margins.

A proper upside case needs segment-level changes, cost savings, implementation time and reinvestment. No future management target, separation multiple or authenticated activist price target is inserted as an existing fact.
docs.D05_market_worries.md:
Title: Cyclicality, project spending and the risk of misreading a peer gap
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2969/000119312513166085/d526189dex991.htm; https://www.fool.com/investing/general/2013/04/24/air-products--chemicals-increases-sales-but-misse.aspx; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2969/000119312512476878/d409668d10k.htm
Date: 2013-04-24

The latest report does not describe a robust synchronized industrial recovery. McGlade cites slower US growth, European contraction, softness in China and an electronics market weaker than expected. Positive acquisition contributions obscure weak existing-business volumes.

The April24 S&P Capital IQ-based earnings recap reports sales below analyst estimates and Q3 guidance below its cited EPS consensus. Those observations provide a plausible market worry: investments and acquisitions may not generate near-term growth sufficient to justify the capital committed.

Pension expense, acquisition integration, energy/distribution costs and customer outages affect margins. An analyst must distinguish costs management can sustainably remove from cyclical weakness or unavoidable supply/service obligations. Cutting capacity or maintenance aggressively could impair the very reliability that makes industrial gases attractive.

The latest company release points to a project backlog aboveUS$3 billion. Backlog supports future revenue opportunities, but also requires capital, execution and customer credit. Long-term contracts help defend returns but do not make construction overruns or a bad contract price harmless.

Fiscal2012 non-GAAP capital expenditures of US$2.778 billion far exceed simple cash plant spending. Indura and other acquisition activity add exposure and integration work. A purchase funded with debt may lift sales while depressing returns if the price or capital requirements are too high.

Portfolio complexity is another concern. Merchant distribution, large tonnage plants, electronics materials and equipment projects need different performance metrics. A centralized structure can dilute accountability, but decentralization is only a potential analytical remedy, not a documented completed change.

The countercase is durable customer relationships, essential products and visible opportunities for productivity. The existing company already reports cost savings and positive pricing in parts of Merchant. An investment need not assume a macro boom if specific operating and capital improvements can be established.

No authenticated public pre-July15 demand for a named CEO or promised margin target is available. A good thesis must identify what a different operator would actually do, the limits imposed by mix, and the returns on retained capital. “Praxair earns more” is an important clue, not a full executable plan.
docs.D06_peer_and_industry_benchmarks.md:
Title: Praxair supplies a demanding but imperfect operating benchmark
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/884905/000115752313001940/a50616772-ex991.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2969/000119312513166085/d526189dex991.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2969/000119312512476878/d409668d10k.htm
Date: 2013-04-24

Praxair's calendarQ1 and APD's fiscalQ2 both end March31 2013, making this a date-aligned operating comparison. Adjusted definitions still require reconciliation.

| Quarter ended March31 | Air Products | Praxair |
|---|---:|---:|
| Sales, US$m | 2,484 | 2,888 |
| Operating profit used, US$m | 390 | 623 adjusted |
| Operating margin used | 15.7% | 21.6% adjusted |
| Diluted EPS used | 1.37 continuing | 1.38 adjusted |
| Annual EPS guidance | 5.45–5.60 adjusted | 5.90–6.05 adjusted |

Praxair reported operating profit is US$600 million and EPS US$1.30. Its adjustments remove a US$23 million Venezuela currency-devaluation charge. Comparing its adjusted21.6% margin with APD's clean current-quarter measure gives an approximately590-basis-point observed gap, not a verified achievable target.

Praxair says comparable sales rose4% after currency, energy pass-through and working-day effects; reported growth is2%. It also faces weaker Europe and moderated North America. Its higher profitability therefore cannot be dismissed solely as benefiting from an entirely different global cycle.

Q1 Praxair CFO is US$472 million and capex US$466 million, primarily new plants under long-term contracts. Its NuCO2 acquisition adds approximatelyUS$1.098 billion acquisition spending. Even a stronger peer requires substantial investment; high margins do not automatically mean immediate distributable cash.

Praxair reports after-tax return on capital13.3% under its own methodology. APD's FY2012 adjusted return on capital employed is11.5%, not necessarily the same definition or period. A standardized asset, tax and lease bridge is needed before treating the difference as a precise ROIC target.

Other global competitors include Air Liquide and Linde, with different currencies, business mixes and geographic exposure. Clean matched quarter multiples and fully reconciled return metrics for all are not provided. No fabricated market-average valuation is used.

The comparison supports a focused diligence program: distribution density, local pricing, overhead, project selection, customer contracts and business mix. It does not establish that selling every nongas asset or replacing management will automatically produce Praxair economics. The capital intensity and implementation risks remain part of the security's valuation.
docs.D07_recent_event_timeline.md:
Title: Investment spending and cost discipline precede the next earnings test
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2969/000119312512476878/d409668d10k.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2969/000119312513166085/d526189dex991.htm; https://investors.airproducts.com/news-releases/news-release-details/air-products-extends-prismr-hydrogen-generator-product-line
Date: 2013-06-24

**Fiscal2012 — acquisition and restructuring year.** Air Products acquires Indura, expands its industrial-gas footprint and incurs significant restructuring charges. The annual financials distinguish GAAP operating margin13.3% from adjusted16.0%. Capital spending including acquisitions and capital leases is unusually high.

**November2012 — audited annual filing.** Investors can inspect segment mix, capital deployment and a long record of dividends. The business is profitable but its adjusted margin is essentially unchanged from2011 despite growth investment. No later disposed-business perimeter is used in this snapshot.

**Early2013 — portfolio and cost actions.** The company continues its announced exit from polyurethane intermediates and pursues productivity. This can reduce revenue while improving focus; a shrinking sales line is not always evidence of deteriorating customer demand.

**April23 — fiscalQ2 results.** Sales rise6% but underlying sales fall2%. Adjusted/continuing EPS isUS$1.37, with15.7% operating margin. Management describes difficult demand in several regions and electronics, while highlighting cost performance and a backlog aboveUS$3 billion.

**April23 — outlook and dividend.** Annual adjusted EPS guidance isUS$5.45–US$5.60 and Q3 US$1.33–US$1.38. The quarterly dividend has increased11% toUS$0.71, extending more than30 years of increases. Dividends are a policy choice supported by cash, not a substitute for attractive capital returns.

**April24 — peer report.** Praxair reports21.6% adjusted operating margin despite its own demand challenges. This provides contemporaneous evidence of a profitability difference worth investigating.

**June24 — product extension.** Air Products announces expanded PRISM hydrogen-generator capacity for on-site customers. It describes leveraging proprietary reformer/purification technology and a global service network. The release is evidence of technical capability, not an earnings forecast for the entire enterprise.

The next quarterly update is still pending at July15. Important tests include underlying volumes, new project start-ups, cash conversion and acquisition returns. No subsequent takeover defense, public shareholder stake, named replacement CEO or new margin target is an established event in these documents.

A possible engagement thesis should be built from the company's disclosed problems and implementable changes, not from knowledge of who will later run the business or which assets will later leave it.
docs.D08_pershing_square_context.md:
Title: A public unnamed-target solicitation and concentrated existing holdings
Source: compiled from: https://www.foxbusiness.com/markets/pershing-square-looks-to-raise-1-billion-for-bet-on-unnamed-company; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1336528/0001172661-13-000908.txt
Date: 2013-07-08

Reuters's July8 report says Pershing Square, approximatelyUS$12 billion manager AUM, is seekingUS$1 billion for new co-investment vehicles PS V and PS V International. The target company is explicitly unnamed. This is public capacity/strategy information, not permission to reveal its later identity.

Ackman's quoted description is a business “simple, predictable, and free-cash-flow-generative and enjoys high barriers to entry.” He says it trades at a “substantially lower multiple of earnings than its most comparable competitor.” Investors are asked to commit byJuly17 and fund byJuly19, with one unnamed institution reportedly ready forUS$200 million.

The source signals willingness to make a large investment and use dedicated vehicles. It does not establish that all requested money has arrived, nor disclose a named operating plan or a verified NAV percentage.

The latest 13F, March31 filedMay15, totalsUS$10.068071 billion table value. Major aggregated common holdings are Canadian PacificUS$3.152141 billion, P&GUS$2.153588 billion, GGPUS$1.485707 billion, BeamUS$1.322811 billion, Burger KingUS$732.908 million and JCPUS$590.435 million.

Howard Hughes isUS$299.036 million, MondelezUS$183.016 million and MatsonUS$74.636 million. P&G calls addUS$73.793 million underlying-share value; that is not option premium or a conventional NAV weight. Sole/shared rows are summed once.

June holdings are not public yet. The March filing excludes shorts, cash and certain other interests; it is not available capital. Existing concentration means a large new position must be evaluated against both portfolio risk and organizational attention.

Canadian Pacific provides a public example of operating activism and leadership focus. JCP and the disputed Herbalife short represent ongoing difficult campaigns, not proof every management-change or public-pressure thesis succeeds. A gas company should be assessed on its own contracts, assets and operating levers.

The pre-cutoff unnamed letter suggests a style of opportunity but cannot substitute for independent analysis of Air Products. No authenticated named APD recommendation or detailed proposal by Ackman is included here. A later disclosure must not be used as an answer embedded in the pack.

drivers.driver: Quality industrial-gas franchise with durable barriers and capacity to improve without relying on a stronger economy.
drivers.quote: APD’s business is extremely high-quality, reasonably priced and run by outstanding management.

drivers.driver: Install a capable operating leader; Seifi Ghasemi appointedJuly1 2014, not a known result in2013.
drivers.quote: Seifi is the ideal leader to transform Air Products

drivers.driver: Close margin gap through overhead and productivity, with later approximately16% to22.5% benchmark against Praxair. This is a2014–15 campaign update, not authenticated July2013 target.
Decentralized accountability, incentive alignment and noncore separation improve focus and returns.

answer_key.pack_quality_notes: Eight docs. Exact original2012 and fiscalQ2 financials, debt addition checked, continuing/total and adjusted EPS separated, contemporaneous Praxair margin, dated analyst estimates, public unnamed fundraising. Unknown rolling extrema/live consensus and full maintenance-capex/peer valuation remain explicit. Snapshot precedes disclosure, not demonstrably first buy.

valuation.eps_path: Growth from US$5.53 to US$7.50 via margin expansion and efficiency
valuation.downside_case: Valuation compression to 14x P/E if margin gap is structural; downside protected by Tonnage contracts

drivers.driver: A dominant, global industrial gas provider with high barriers to entry and long-term, predictable Tonnage contracts [D01].
Significant operational margin gap versus peers like Praxair indicates latent earnings power that can be unlocked through management focus [D06].
Market misperception of the business as a low-growth commodity player overlooks the potential for significant FCF expansion via portfolio pruning and productivity [D01, D06].
Clear path to EPS growth by closing half the margin gap with industry leaders, driving earnings toward US$7.50 per share [D06].

kill_criteria: Operating margins fail to expand toward 20% over 18 months [D06].
Continued reliance on acquisitions to mask underlying volume declines [D03].
Failure to divest non-core segments as per the productivity plan [D01].
FCF yield fails to improve from 1.2% [D02, D04].
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that the margin gap compared to peers is structural and non-correctable despite management intervention, confirming the business is a low-margin commodity enterprise.
final.memo:
The Company is a dominant provider of industrial gases and technology, operating in a global market with high barriers to entry due to its significant installed assets and deep customer integration [D01]. Despite its market position, the firm currently produces an adjusted operating margin of 16.0%, which lags significantly behind its peer, Praxair, at 21.6% [D02, D06].

We believe the current market valuation reflects a misguided view of the business as a low-growth, capital-intensive commodity producer [D06]. The market is focused on declining underlying volumes and historical margin trends, failing to recognize that the performance gap is largely a function of operational inefficiencies that can be corrected through better portfolio management and increased accountability [D01, D03, D05, D06].

At a purchase price reflecting 17.9x FY2012 earnings, we see a compelling opportunity to drive EPS to US$7.50 by capturing half of the margin delta to our peers and optimizing the US$3 billion backlog [D04, D05, D06]. We anticipate an IRR of 22% as the company transitions toward a more profitable, disciplined operating model with a terminal multiple of 18x [D03, D06].

As active owners, we will engage with management to implement a rigorous productivity plan and portfolio optimization strategy, including the divestment of non-core assets [D01, D06]. Our role is to ensure the conversion of the backlog into high-return cash flows rather than capital-intensive commodity projects [D05].

Our primary risk is that the margin gap is structural and inherent to the asset base, which would limit our upside [D04, D06]. However, the presence of long-term Tonnage contracts provides a stable floor that limits the risk of permanent capital impairment [D01].

We are initiating a 10% position in the Company. We have high conviction that operational discipline will transform the business and deliver superior shareholder returns [D06].

valuation.eps_path: $7.00 - $7.50 EPS by 2016-2017 driven by margin expansion and productivity
valuation.downside_case: Limited downside due to long-term tonnage gas contracts and high infrastructure barriers

drivers.driver: Air Products is a dominant provider of industrial gases with high barriers to entry and long-duration, defensive customer relationships [D01].
A persistent 600bps operating margin gap compared to peer Praxair represents a significant, fixable opportunity for earnings growth [D06].
We can drive value by advocating for portfolio rationalization, disciplined capital allocation, and operational efficiency [D01, D06].
At 17.9x FY2012 earnings, the stock is attractively priced for a high-quality infrastructure business undergoing a transformation [D04].

kill_criteria: Operating margins fail to show sustained expansion toward the 20%+ benchmark over four consecutive quarters
Management persists with high-capex, low-return project growth instead of pivoting to FCF optimization
Return on Invested Capital (ROIC) fails to improve as portfolio rationalization progresses
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that the current profitability deficit is structural and tied to the inherent nature of the assets rather than management underperformance.
final.memo:
Air Products and Chemicals is a dominant infrastructure player in the industrial gases industry, benefiting from long-duration customer relationships and significant barriers to entry [D01]. Despite the essential nature of its business, the firm has failed to achieve the profitability levels of its peers [D06]. We believe this gap is not structural but the result of insufficient management focus on operational discipline and capital allocation [D01, D06].

The opportunity exists because the market incorrectly views the firm's current underperformance as permanent [D05, D06]. While underlying sales growth has been soft, we see a clear path to mid-teens EPS growth through margin expansion and improved capital efficiency [D01, D03, D06]. We believe the firm can close the 600bps operating margin gap to best-in-class peer Praxair through aggressive portfolio rationalization [D01, D06].

We are able to acquire our stake at 17.9x FY2012 adjusted earnings, a valuation that does not reflect the earnings power of a fully optimized industrial gas franchise [D04]. With margin improvement initiatives, we expect to see EPS of $7.00 to $7.50 by 2016-2017 [D01, D06]. This path, combined with a rerating of the multiple as the company transitions to a more disciplined cash-flow-generative profile, supports an expected annual return of over 20% [D03, D04].

As active shareholders, we intend to engage with the Board to accelerate the transition to a more efficient operating model [D06]. We will push for a strategic review of all non-core assets and advocate for a change in capital allocation policy to maximize free cash flow conversion rather than prioritizing high-capex growth [D01, D02, D04]. We are prepared to advocate for new leadership or board members if the current team cannot demonstrate meaningful improvement in operating margins [D06].

The risks are mitigated by the long-term, contractual nature of the tonnage gas segment, which provides a durable floor for the business [D01]. While the company's capital intensity remains a challenge, we are confident that a focus on productivity can mitigate this issue [D02, D06]. We will monitor progress closely and change our view if we conclude that the current profitability gap is deeply embedded in the company's asset base and beyond management's control.

We are initiating a position today with an intent to scale to 12% of NAV as we engage with management to unlock this value [D04, D08]. This represents a high-conviction bet on the ability to transform an underperforming, yet high-quality, industrial asset into a best-in-class performer [D06].
